label: Wheat Prices Keep Falling
detail: Wheat prices fall steadily through October 1896 instead of recovering, deepening farmers' distress just before the vote.
assumption: Farmers and rural voters in wheat-growing states, especially the Midwest and West, are more receptive to the party urging currency expansion and less persuaded that prosperity is returning; urban and eastern voters are barely affected.
facts_text: Wheat prices at Chicago and New York have kept falling through October, with no autumn recovery in the market.
Farmers across the wheat belt report that the price of their crop is lower than at harvest time last year, and that mortgage and debt burdens are heavier as a result.
research_questions: How did farm county vote shifts in 1896 correlate with local wheat price changes during the autumn?
Did farmers who were in debt or mortgaged vote differently from debt-free farmers in the same counties in 1896?
How did the rise in wheat prices in autumn 1896 affect rural support for free silver in the Midwest?
source_text: Wheat prices keep falling through October 1896 instead of rising.
